messages:
jamie: quick heads-up — noticed PR #421 merged at 11:12 but the apply never ran before ArgoCD picked up the change. resulted in a brief drift + rollback. anyone seen this race between GH auto-merge, Atlantis apply, and ArgoCD sync?

hannah: ugh, can you drop the PR link and the atlantis comment thread?

jamie: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/421 and the atlantis comment is below. looks like GH auto-merge was on (label-based), merged, and the new commit triggered ArgoCD sync before the atlantis apply commit landed. logs: 
```
GitHub: Merge commit created (merge queue) at 11:12
ArgoCD: detected commit xyz at 11:13 and started sync
Atlantis: queued apply, but apply runner picked it up at 11:14 (after sync)
Result: app rolled back because env var missing until apply completed
```

rafael: yeah that timing can happen when we let merges bypass status checks (auto-merge + label). Two quick options: block merge until atlantis apply status exists, or have a post-merge hook that pauses ArgoCD until apply completes.

ops-bot: atlantis comment: "Atlantis plan performed. Apply pending: run 'atlantis apply' or comment 'atlantis apply'" (comment timestamp 11:12:40). No check-run created for apply success in this repo.

ci-robot: fyi we can create a GitHub Check Run that marks infra/apply:success when Atlantis finishes. GH Branch protection can require that check.

hannah: I like the check-run approach. Rafael — any quick sketch of the action?

rafael: short sketch: add a minimal GH Action that listens for atlantis webhook (or comment) and when apply completes it calls the Checks API. Then require the check in branch protection. Example snippet: 
```yaml
name: atlantis-apply-status
on: repository_dispatch
jobs:
  mark-apply:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: mark check run
        uses: actions/github-script@v6
        with:
          script: |
            const res = await github.checks.create({
              owner: context.repo.owner, repo: context.repo.repo, name: 'infra/apply', head_sha: process.env.SHA, status: 'completed', conclusion: 'success'
            })
```
Note: we'll need Atlantis to emit the commit SHA it applied (it does in logs).

jamie: alternate short-term fix: disable auto-merge and require manual merge after apply comment. not ideal for velocity but safer.

hannah: agree — let's do a two-step plan: 1) disable auto-merge for infra/* branches (ops) today, 2) add the GH Action to create infra/apply check and require it in branch protection (rafael can open the PR).

rafael: I'll open a PR for the action + branch-protection change. will add a lightweight retry to avoid flakiness.

jamie: thanks. i'll turn off auto-merge on the repo now and post here when done. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: auto-merge disabled for redwood-inference/infra at 11:35 PT (by jamie).

jamie: done. I'll watch the next merges and report if any oddness. thanks all.
